title: Introduce fidelity-weighted-span-summarizer and rule-based alert quieting
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Adds a fidelity-weighted span summarizer that produces compact, scored summaries for sampled traces and a rule-based alert quieting layer that suppresses noisy alerts during known benign windows. Motivation: Our alert queues and trace retention costs are dominated by high-fidelity traces for a small fraction of invocations. We need a mechanism to (1) keep high-fidelity data for anomalous or high-impact requests, (2) retain succinct but informative summaries for the long tail, and (3) reduce alert churn by applying contextual suppression rules for predictable noise (scheduled jobs, bulk imports, retry storms).

Design/approach: The span summarizer runs in the observability pipeline after span enrichment. It scores spans using a fidelity metric composed of: token-phase variance, invocation error tags, kernel-contention markers, and a small ML binary classifier trained on historical RCA-labeled traces (model packaged as a light feature hash). The summarizer outputs a short text summary, an 8-character fingerprint, and a fidelity score. Summaries are persisted to the compact-invocation-index and included as the primary payload for sampled traces when fidelity < threshold. Fidelity thresholds and score weights are configurable per-tenant via the observability config API.

The alert quieting subsystem introduces a rule engine that consumes metadata (route, tenant labels, scheduled-window tags, burst-score) and emits suppression windows for alerts at the routing layer. Rules are prioritized and can be temporary (duration) or tied to causal markers (e.g., maintenance flag). We ship a small default rule set that quiets alerts for predictable periodic batch windows and de-duplicates alerts that originate from dependent downstream failures.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core summarizer implementation and feature extraction pipeline.
- [x] Compact summary schema and index writer.
- [x] Config API (read/write) and per-tenant thresholds.
- [x] Rule engine and default rule set.
- [x] End-to-end integration tests and load bench.
- [x] Observability dashboards: Summaries explorer and Quieting audit panel.
- [x] Backwards-compatible: old sampled-trace consumers still receive full spans when fidelity >= threshold.

Testing & performance: Integration test harness includes synthetic injection of 15k traces/min with a 5% anomalous class. Summarizer CPU cost: ~8% increase on pipeline workers at p95 load; tail latency impact on span ingestion < 45ms p95 (within SLO). Benchmarks included in this PR (scripts/benchmarks/fidelity_summarizer) reproduce these numbers. We added golden tests for summary content and fingerprint stability.

Review conversation snippets: 
- Arjun: "Can we avoid touching hot code paths in span ingestion? I want a microbenchmark showing p99 tail impact."
  - Author: "Moved feature extraction to a bounded worker pool and added the benchmark script; p99 delta measured at +11ms locally."
- Sofia: "How do we prevent quieting rules from hiding real incidents?"
  - Author: "Rules are opt-in per-tenant by default and every suppression creates an auditable 'quieting token' visible in Quieting audit panel; we included safety checks for overlapping rules and automatic expiration."
- Daniel: "Where is the ML classifier coming from? We need reproducibility and a small fallback."
  - Author: "Classifier is a light logistic-regression trained offline; model weights are checked into observability/models with a reproducible training config. If the model fails the summarizer falls back to a deterministic heuristic score."

CI summary: Initial CI run: lint failed (flake8 rule on single-quoted f-strings) -> fixed. Unit tests: all pass. Integration tests: one flaky integration test (span-serializer) retried and passed on rerun. Load bench artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/pr-772424/bench-2025-10-20.tar.gz. Final CI status: pass.

Merge & rollout: Merged to main via squash on 2025-10-22 (merge commit sha: 3adf9b7c1a4b2f6e8d7f5e9b1219c0a8f6d7f3b2). Rollout plan: staged rollout to observability-plane nodes using the existing canary policy: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 48h with monitoring gates. We added automatic rollback conditions: if summarizer CPU > 20% delta or alert false-suppression rate > 0.5% within any 15m window.

Notes for oncall: runbook updated at runbooks/observability/quieting.md. If noisy alerts persist after rollout, toggle observability.config:quieting.default_rules=false to disable the default rule set. For debugging sample summaries, use the Summaries explorer dashboard to fetch the full trace using the summary fingerprint.
